unplaced.description: A supernova remnant and pulsar wind nebula roughly 25 light-years in radius, centered on the Lighthouse. Its shifting filaments affect navigation across Collective space. The nebula spans multiple regions and is not represented as a separate administrative region.

traga.name: Traga Expanse
traga.subtitle: The Collective’s heartland
traga.description: Fifteen systems surround the federal capital at Elysium. The synth and Ceph worlds anchor a region of settlement, agriculture and interstellar institutions. Local arrangement follows the Codex’s Traga chart.

aradian.name: Aradian Flow
aradian.subtitle: Industry, agriculture and the Lighthouse
aradian.description: Twenty charted systems include Corinth, Karnaka Prime and the Lighthouse. The Sevore, Vaedim, Rennick and Oson industrial base supports the Collective, while nebular filaments complicate shockpoint navigation.

arvis.name: Arvis Gulf
arvis.subtitle: Human settlement and the forge worlds
arvis.description: The territorial register places Hypatia, Viric Prime, Zha’Koth’Mar, Meyra, Calvea, Felwinter and Drifthold here. The region article has not yet been written; marker positions are schematic and no territorial boundary is established.

spinward.name: Spinward Expanse
spinward.subtitle: The threshold of the Great Wildlands
spinward.description: One of the Collective’s two documented approaches to the Great Wildlands. Calmore contains Synil and its inhabited resort moon Aurallux. The territory register places Synil in this region; Aurallux’s older infobox calls its locality the Tsyresi Adjunct Zone. No complete regional chart is published.

drayson.name: Drayson Hinterlands
drayson.subtitle: Contested rimward frontier
drayson.description: The frontier bordering UACS space and opening toward the Great Wildlands. Prathia was annexed by Kadaym in 129 CE; destroyed Kevak jumpgates and Silent incursions have isolated the region. The chart contains 23 systems including independent Montressor; the region article counts 22.

presentation.notesHTML:
Elysian Stellar Atlas · 134 CE. Shared atlas framework with Kadaym and IULR navigation and orbital-display improvements. Codex sources reviewed 1 November 2026.

Explore

Drag to pan; scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose a regional chart in the dropdown, or click open regional space to highlight it without moving the camera. Overview names appear at 220% (160% in a highlighted region); planet sublabels at 320% (220% highlighted). Regional charts and their widgets show active names at 64% and sublabels at 80%; neighboring names at 80% and sublabels at 125%. All thresholds are inclusive. These base percentages apply to chart areas at least 640 pixels wide and 360 pixels tall; smaller charts multiply them by the greater of 640 / width or 360 / height, rounded up, so labels have comparable room. The zoom readout always uses the same scale as the visibility checks. Labels controls all map inscriptions. The Index starts collapsed and retains your choice during navigation. A single marker click opens a dossier; double-click a star to open its system, then double-click a planet to explore its moons and stations. Index and Dossier panels collapse independently. Escape returns to the parent view; arrow keys pan, +/− zoom and 0 fits the chart.

Source coverage

All five named regions are represented. Traga, Aradian and Drayson preserve the relative system arrangements in their published charts. The joined heartland silhouette, shared edges and spacing are illustrative, not newly established borders. Drayson joins the Collective through Aradian Flow. Its damaged jumpgate connections and recorded disruption do not imply a detached territorial region. Arvis and Spinward use schematic arrangements of documented systems. The national totals—463 controlled systems, 57 inhabited planets and an approximately 63-light-year span—are not a count of the individually charted objects. Decorative background stars are not additional catalogue entries.

The Lighthouse Nebula is a physical nebula spanning regional boundaries, not a sixth administrative region. Its pulsar and Core Array belong to Aradian Flow. Neither region outlines nor nebular backgrounds define travel distances, safe radiation limits or routes.

Preserved distinctions

Prathia is a Kadaymian holding in the Drayson Hinterlands. Montressor is independent CONCORD territory. The region’s article counts 22 systems, while its chart labels 23 including Montressor. A catalogue does not imply uncontested ownership or current habitability.

Elysium’s own infobox gives 12.3 billion inhabitants; the older territorial table says 12.1 billion. The atlas uses the own-article value. Keyhaul Trench’s infobox uses “Kevak Adjunct Zone,” while its prose and territorial register place it in Drayson. Aurallux uses “Tsyresi Adjunct Zone” in its older infobox, while Synil is assigned to Spinward Expanse in the register. Karnak’s system infobox retains “Karnak Adjunct Zone”; the regional chart places it in Aradian Flow. These local designations remain visible in live dossiers.

Aradian Flow dates Sigma Aradis V’s destruction to 65 CE; the territory register dates its glassing to 67 CE. Both are retained. Cellis Prime’s article identifies Ceph and Karkarian origins there, while Keyhaul Trench is also described as the Karkarian homeworld; each world retains its source wording.

Orbital diagrams

All displayed planets are selectable at full brightness. Catalogue designations remain until a matching Codex article exists. The atlas follows redirects and remembers article page IDs, allowing labels and links to follow subsequent article moves. Planet records keep stable internal identifiers so saved routes and moon relationships survive renames. Asterisks mark schematic orbital ordering. Additional planets, moons and local stations extend the documented register for exploration. Benthos and Aurallux are inhabited moons. Exact orbital radii, phases, speeds and stellar motions are illustrative. The Lighthouse beam is slowed for legibility. Station hosts include documented relationships and atlas expansions; facilities with unknown hosts remain in the system’s unlocated register. The Core Array’s schematic orbit represents a distributed installation.

Widgets and exact links

Circa’s Triad has a selectable exterior schematic from its Station overview button, with a replayable build and component descriptions. Use ?system=columa&object=Circa%27s%20Triad&station=1&view=widget for its schematic widget. Use ?region=traga&view=widget, ?system=lighthouse&view=widget, or ?planet=Elysium&view=widget. Other region keys are aradian, arvis, spinward and drayson. Full-view links preserve the exact object and viewing mode. Widget symbols and labels open Codex articles, and do not switch views on double-click. MediaWiki EmbedMap can pass the same query through window.SKYRIVER_ATLAS_QUERY before initialization.

Live dossiers and offline use

Planet article titles refresh across the atlas and its widgets on opening, every minute, and when returning to the tab. A first rename must retain a redirect from the catalogue designation until the atlas has discovered the article. Last confirmed names are retained offline where browser storage is available. Population, capital, sovereignty and other available facts refresh from each object’s own article on opening, every minute while visible, on returning to the tab, or with Refresh data. Both current InfoboxNeue and older infobox formats are supported. Missing articles retain the atlas record; failed network checks retain the last available data. Bundled article images work offline. Forge and Karnak currently store their system infoboxes on the unsuffixed article; their dossier data reads those pages while Go to System still targets the distinct System article.
